headline: BEST EVER HOLE: GR Silver Drills 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag at San Marcial — Shatters Previous Records
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) hit its best-ever intercept at the San Marcial project in Mexico — 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag including a jaw-dropping 8.25m at 8,579 g/t Ag in hole SMS26-04. Two rigs are currently on site in a 20,000m step-out campaign with additional rigs en route; a resource update is expected H2 2026.

headline: SURFACE OXIDE DISCOVERY: Collective Mining Hits 71m at 1.95 g/t AuEq at Northern Apollo — New Open-Pit Target in Colombia
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) announced a new precious metal-rich oxide zone at Northern Apollo, Colombia — 700m of strike, 200m wide, up to 100m deep, outcropping from surface. Best intercept: 71.2m at 1.95 g/t AuEq (from surface). The zone sits north of the main Apollo breccia body and represents a potential open-pittable heap-leach target. The company holds US$113M cash and is ramping to 14 drill rigs.

headline: Troilus Extends West Rim Zone 2.92 g/t AuEQ Over 19m — Outside Current Resource, 200m from Reserve Pit
snippet: Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG) expanded the West Rim Zone at its copper-gold project in northern Quebec, returning 2.92 g/t AuEQ over 19m — best intercept 5.96 g/t AuEq over 6m. All holes sit entirely outside the current mineral resource while within 200m of the planned reserve pit footprint from the 2024 Feasibility Study. Phase 2 drilling is being designed.

headline: NexGold Drills 15.21 g/t Gold Over 20m at Goldlund, Supporting Ontario Resource Expansion
snippet: NexGold Mining (TSXV: NEXG) reported high-grade intercepts at Goldlund — part of the Goliath Gold Complex in northwestern Ontario — including 15.21 g/t gold over 20.1m, 5.11 g/t over 21.8m, and 4.51 g/t over 21.9m. Results confirm mineral resource continuity and support expansion potential at one of Canada's most advanced-stage gold development projects.

headline: Sigma Lithium Fights $10M Brazilian Court Order, Says Ruling Timed to Sabotage Record Earnings
snippet: Sigma Lithium (NASDAQ: SGML) is appealing a May 17 local court order from Aracuai, Brazil requiring a US$10M legal collateral over alleged waste pile damages at the Grota do Cirilo operation. The company called the decision 'unwarranted,' said due process was skipped, and flagged a coordinated 'fake news' campaign coinciding with its record earnings release. Final resolution through Brazil's courts could take years.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,500: JPMorgan Targets $5,055 by Q4 as Institutions Double Their Gold Allocation
snippet: Gold traded at $4,503.89/oz on May 20, down 4.6% over the past month but still 35.7% above year-ago levels. JPMorgan forecasts a Q4 2026 average of $5,055/oz with structural support from persistent central bank buying. Institutions now hold 2.8% of assets in gold — roughly double the share from a decade ago — providing a meaningful demand floor beneath the metal.

headline: URANIUM SUPPLY CRUNCH: EIA Flags 184-Million-Pound U.S. Gap While Big Tech Nuclear Deals Tighten Demand
snippet: Uranium spot eased to $85.25/lb on May 18 — up 24% year-over-year — but the U.S. EIA has flagged a looming 184-million-pound supply gap for American utilities over the next decade, more than three years of reactor consumption. Meta signed agreements for up to 7.8 GW of nuclear capacity and Microsoft locked in 800 MW for AI data centers, reinforcing the structural demand case for uranium equities.

headline: COPPER NEAR RECORD: $6.18/lb on May 20, Up 33.7% Year-Over-Year as Supply Tightness Persists
snippet: Copper hit $6.18 per pound ($13,625/tonne) on May 20, 2026 — up 0.31% on the session and 33.7% above year-ago levels. Chile's Cochilco raised its average 2026 forecast to $5.55/lb, citing firm global demand and structural supply tightness, though spot prices have already far exceeded that average. Sentiment headwinds include soft Chinese retail sales and contracting fixed asset investment.

headline: SILVER'S WILD 2026: $121 ATH in January, $80 Floor in April, Then a 6% Surge on US-China Trade Truce
snippet: Silver hit an all-time high of $121.64 in January 2026 before correcting sharply through April. On May 11 it surged 6% in a single session on a US-China 90-day tariff truce — then pulled back again on sticky inflation data. Analysts note a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit is structural support, but warn retail investors against chasing momentum after 150%-plus year-over-year gains.

headline: MINERS vs METAL: Gold Stocks Poised to Finally Outrun Bullion in 2026 as Valuations Catch Up
snippet: Multiple analysts argue 2026 is the year gold mining equities finally close the valuation gap with the metal — citing operational improvements, sector undervaluation relative to spot gold, and elevated M&A premium potential. With gold up 35% year-over-year and miner margins near historic highs, the case for owning producers over bullion is the strongest it has been in a decade.

headline: NdPr COOLS 21% in April But Western Rare Earth Producers Stay Firmly Profitable at $99/kg
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21.0% in April to $99.61/kg — its sharpest monthly pullback since the Q1 rally began — but the metal remains 88% above its January 2026 open. Western producers including MP Materials and Lynas continue to operate well above their cost bases. U.S. Project Vault ($12B strategic reserve initiative) and strong DoD contracting remain structural tailwinds for domestic rare earth equities.
